notes: A provider of the `decide` inference type: Cloudflare's Clef decision models (clef, 27B, and clef-flash, 9B) on Workers AI, reached at https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4 unless CLOUDFLARE_CLEF_BASE_URL or credentials.cloudflareClef.baseURL names another base, with the account id in the route. The token and account id are CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY and CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID, shared with the `cloudflare` Workers AI text provider, which means an ambient pair from that provider also activates decide here. Tier 3 for the same reasons as typesafe, laya, xor and perplexity-decider (the catalog schema has no decide vocabulary and requires output-token fields), and distinct from the catalog's `cloudflare` provider. Extends SystemOneDecisionProvider, which gained a model argument on decisionEndpoint (the model is in the URL path), a readDecisionPayload hook (Cloudflare wraps every answer in a result envelope) and optional digit, symbol and astral rates on decisionLimits. Declares inferenceKinds ["decide"] and decisionLimits, and sits after perplexity-decider in HAND_DESCRIPTORS so the other four stay the default whenever their keys are set. Reads images (not video) in their own images array. The state limit is 16,000 estimated tokens (at most about 18,400 real ones), inside what the Workers AI endpoint read in full on 2026-10-07 (at least 190,153 tokens on clef-flash, 52,154 on clef) and a bounded wait for a fail-open consumer; until 2026-10-04 the endpoint ignored text past about 2,048 tokens without an error and the limit was 1,500 (hosted service or model: unknown). The default timeout is 5 s plus 250 ms for each full 1,000 estimated state tokens; the encoded request cap remains 256,000 bytes. Follow-up on 2026-10-04 used 133 serial probe calls: both models accepted 520,000 text characters and refused 525,000 with 413/code 5021, on 2026-10-03, clef-flash alone accepted 262,000 and refused 270,000. Refusal estimates match encoded body characters / 4, rounded up; the threshold moved from 65,527 accepted / 67,527 refused to 130,026 accepted / 131,276 refused (clef) and 130,027 / 131,277 (clef-flash). The error still prints 65,536; inference: the new interval contains 131,072, twice that figure. The reason is unknown. Four images and image/jpg were accepted; the alias is normalized to image/jpeg. Both models read facts at the original clef-flash lower bounds for logs, number lists, digit arrays and compact JSON, but not about 2.5% further on. Those checks, natural scripts on clef and a many-key object on both fit the existing rates. The object control failed three times and passed after an explicit field-name question and zero-padded keys were introduced together. Current image-byte limits remain unmeasured; the local 256,000-byte cap with images is not live-tested. Three live canaries (19.10, 19.10b and 19.11) detect changes in state or request behavior; 19.11 checks the text-only service ceiling on clef-flash. Follow-up on 2026-10-04 used 133 serial probe calls: both models accepted 520,000 text characters and refused 525,000 with 413/code 5021, on 2026-10-03, clef-flash alone accepted 262,000 and refused 270,000. Refusal estimates are the encoded body bytes / 4 (rounded up in seven of eight refusals, one lower in the eighth); the threshold moved from 65,527 accepted / 67,527 refused to 130,026 accepted / 131,276 refused (clef) and 130,027 / 131,277 (clef-flash). The error still prints 65,536; inference: the new interval contains 131,072, twice that figure. The reason is unknown. Four images and image/jpg were accepted; the alias is normalized to image/jpeg. Both models read facts at the original clef-flash lower bounds for logs, number lists, digit arrays and compact JSON, but not 2.5% to 3.1% further on. Those checks, natural scripts on clef and a many-key object on both fit the existing rates. The object control failed three times and passed after an explicit field-name question and zero-padded keys were introduced together. On 2026-10-05 both models accepted PNG request bodies up to 492,485 bytes and refused 532,505 bytes (clef-flash) and 532,499 (clef) with 413/code 5021, well above the local 256,000-byte cap; live case 19.14 sends an image request just under that cap. On 2026-10-05 the account's Free plan daily allocation ran out and Cloudflare answered 429 with code 4006, which is not retried. On 2026-10-07 the endpoint read states of at least 190,153 tokens on clef-flash and 52,154 on clef (clef answered HTTP 529, code 5012, for the 190,153-token array), where on 2026-10-03 and 2026-10-04 it read only about 2,048. Live canaries 19.10 and 19.10b check that a state just under NeuroLink's own limit is read to its end by both models; 19.11 checks the text-only service ceiling on clef-flash.
